# Align package validation with source-only npm releases

## Context

The operator's release decision is recorded on [#18823](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18823#issuecomment-6016025585): generated browser bundles do not belong in the npm package; consuming workspaces generate them. The publisher already runs `npm ci` → `npm publish` on a fresh checkout.

This is the implementation follow-up proposed there. The older Mermaid-only decision body remains historical context; this leaf has one package-policy cleanup scope.

Design authority: the operator's October 6 no-generated-bundles decision, as recorded by Grace in the linked receipt.

## The Problem

Validation still certifies a different package:

- `.npmignore` re-includes generated parser, diagram, editor and highlighting bundles.
- `check-package-contents.mjs` requires 13 generated `dist/` entries.
- Package-content and consumer-runtime workflows generate them before packing.

A direct rule probe at `6e19f603` accepts `dist/parse5.mjs` and `dist/monaco/editor.mjs`, while a source-only path set reports all 13 bundle files missing. A developer's already-built checkout can therefore pack generated files even though a clean publisher does not.

## The Architectural Reality

Existing owners:

- `.npmignore` plus `buildScripts/util/npmIgnoreComposition.mjs` govern the actual npm file set.
- `buildScripts/util/check-package-contents.mjs` audits that file set; its owning spec is `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/checkPackageContents.spec.mjs`.
- `buildScripts/util/check-consumer-runtime-build.mjs` packs and installs a real consumer fixture, then compiles Data, Canvas, App and Main contexts.
- `buildScripts/util/browserBundles.mjs` identifies build/copy producers; its comments still describe shipping their output.
- The two named CI workflows decide whether generation happens before or after package installation.

No new module, service, build primitive or publisher step is needed. The existing consumer fixture is the right place to prove generation and compilation outside the producer checkout.

## The Fix

1. Exclude the whole generated `dist/` tree, including outputs already present in a developer checkout.
2. Replace required-generated-file assertions with a forbidden-`dist/` assertion; retain private-state exclusion and ontology carve-out coverage.
3. Pack the source-only package in both checks. In the consumer check, install the installed Engine's build dependencies without lifecycle side effects, then run its existing bundle-generation command inside that installed copy before compilation.
4. Update directly affected comments/tests so they describe source delivery and consumer generation.

| Surface | Source of authority | Behavior | Failure | Documentation | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| npm file set | Operator ruling; `.npmignore` composition | No `dist/` file ships, built checkout or clean | Package guard fails on any generated entry | Ignore header and guard JSDoc | Real pack with planted generated files |
| Package guard | Existing prefix validator and own spec | Enforce generated-tree exclusion alongside existing private-state rules | Nonzero exit on a forbidden entry | Guard output/JSDoc | Negative rule control and real pack |
| Consumer build | Existing installed-fixture guard | Generate dependencies in the installed Engine, then preserve all current compile/context assertions | Dependency generation or compile failure fails the job | Consumer guard/workflow comments | Actual CI consumer fixture |

Decision Record impact: none; applies the existing release ruling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An actual npm pack excludes every `dist/` path even when generated files exist locally; source, producer scripts and existing privacy exclusions remain correct.
- [ ] The package guard rejects representative parser/editor/highlighting files and an unknown future `dist/` path; its existing private-state/carve-out controls remain green.
- [ ] Neither check workflow generates bundles in the producer checkout before packing.
- [ ] The consumer fixture generates its installed Engine's browser dependencies and passes its existing Data, Canvas, App and Main compilation/context controls.
- [ ] Obsolete required-generated-file tests and shipment claims are removed or updated; no publisher, release version or scaffold publish step changes.

## Out of Scope

Publishing Engine or create-app, changing the accepted package decision, redesigning the bundlers, unrelated package-size cuts, and native Fleet installation.

## Avoided Traps

Do not revive the deliberately closed `#19423` publisher build step. Do not certify only a clean checkout: generated files must be present to falsify the ignore rule. Do not copy this checkout's prebuilt bundles into the consumer fixture.

Related: #18823, neomjs/create-app#34.
